title.narrative: First Panama Fiscal Management and Growth DPL

description.narrative: The DPL supports Panama's efforts to (i) enhance fiscal sustainability and the efficiency of fiscal management; and (ii) mobilize private investment, with emphasis on infrastructure and in natural assets.

The development objective of the First Panama Fiscal Management and Growth Development Policy Financing for Panama is to support Panama's efforts to: (i) enhance fiscal sustainability and the efficiency of fiscal management; and (ii) mobilize private investment, with emphasis on infrastructure and in natural assets. The development policy financing (DPF) series, including this operation, is closely aligned with Panama's Strategic Plan 2025-2029 (PSP), which targets high growth and job creation through four main objectives: (i) fostering investment and job creation in key sectors; (ii) expanding opportunities via quality education and basic services; (iii) strengthening institutions and government efficiency; and (iv) promoting environmental sustainability and sound natural resource management. Pillar 1 supports PSP's third objective by strengthening fiscal institutions and promoting more efficient fiscal management. Pillar 2 advances PSP objectives (i) and (iv) by encouraging private investment across various economic sectors, including infrastructure and natural resource management (under DPFs two and three).

Fiber to the Home Broad Band (FTTH) penetration (percent of households with access)

comment.narrative: Data under review. The baseline of 24% (590,546 households, Dec. 2024) does not appear fully consistent with ASEP data reporting 743,910 fixed broadband subscribers and 761,851 internet subscribers for the same period. The discrepancy likely reflects differences in definitions (e.g., subscribers vs. household connections, fixed broadband vs. FTTH-specific coverage). The team is coordinating with MEF and ASEP to confirm the exact definition and methodology before any adjustment is made.

PPPs payments as share of total public investments spending

comment.narrative: Availability payments for the already awarded projects for the Panamerican Road East and West (both brownfield) are expected to begin in 2027, with payments for other projects in the structuring pipeline envisaged for 2028 onwards (e.g. Centenario Highway and Northern Corridor). The DPL supports PA#6 (Executive Decree No. 58 of 2025), which shortened the PPP structuring cycle by removing duplicative pre-feasibility requirements and aligning PPP projects with strategic plans. Subsequent triggers will strengthen the PPP fiscal management framework through methodologies to record and manage PPP commitments, reforms to payment modalities, and a Multi-Year Investment Programming System. The ex-ante PCE estimate is US$760.4 million, based on 4 Phase 2 projects (Autopista Arraiján-La Chorrera y Via Centenario, Corredor Norte David, Variante de PenonomE, and Ciudad Judicial) with a total investment of US$2,534.6 million and a 30% attribution rate. Sources: MEF; SNAPP; MFMod.

title.narrative: Public debt transactions in Panama's stock exchange secondary market (OTC and REPOS), millons

comment.narrative: Progress is noted. The MEF provided the data for the the period of May 2025 to May 2026 of USD209 million. The team is working with the Ministry of Economy and Finance and the Panama Stock Exchange (Latinex) to monitor target transaction volumes, as well as to track growth in the number of market participants. Sources: Latinex Volume per Issuer (www.latinexbolsa.com) and the Ministry of Economy and Finance Report "Informe de Transacciones OTC con Bonos de la República."

title.narrative: Cumulative amount of financing mobilized through VCCs, domestically or overseas, million.

comment.narrative: There were no carbon market reforms under DPO1 and the planned trigger has not been enacted yet, hence, the measurement of new issuance under the new rules for carbon markets is not yet relevant. The Voluntary Carbon Market (VCM) framework is a topic to be discussed with the authorities in the context of future operations. This indicator will be reassessed during the preparation of subsequent DPOs.

Pension income gender gap (women/men pension income ratio)

comment.narrative: Updated data for this indicator is not yet available. The team contacted the Caja de Seguro Social de Panamá (CSS) in June 2026 to obtain the current women/men pension income ratio, but the institution confirmed that the analysis has not been conducted and the source of the 2024 baseline figure (0.62) is under review by their actuarial department. The team will follow up with CSS and update this indicator once data is confirmed. No progress rating is assigned for this reporting period.

comment.narrative: Tax revenue as a share of GDP has improved to 7.1% in 2025, with tax revenues growing by 9.0% year-on-year. This was driven by a notable 14.4% increase in direct taxes, with strong collections from payroll income tax, real estate tax, corporate tax, and capital gains tax, reflecting enhanced tax enforcement, greater use of technology, and measures such as the Fiscal Lottery. Source: Ministry of Economy and Finance — Fiscal Balance. https://www.mef.

comment.narrative: As of February 2026, Panama remains on the EU list of non-cooperative jurisdictions for tax purposes (EU blacklist). The next formal EU review is expected in October 2026.
